ordered_diagnoses: Sjögren's Syndrome with Central Nervous System Involvement

s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent episodes of neurological deficits with evidence of inflammation and white matter changes
salient_findings: Mild aphasia and confusion
Sudden-onset right leg weakness
Mild headache and right facial droop
Extensive white matter changes on MRI
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein level
key_facts: History of well-controlled hypertension and hyperlipidemia
On methotrexate and sulfasalazine treatment
Developed mild aphasia and confusion lasting for several hours
Right leg weakness resolved within 2 days
Presented with mild headache and right facial droop
Neurological examination revealed paraphasic errors and word-finding difficulty
Bilateral upgoing plantars
No motor or sensory deficits
Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate and C-reactive protein level
High titer of cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody
CSF analysis showed 12/µL white blood cell count and 4 oligoclonal bands
MRI Brain showed extensive white matter changes with enhancement along the arachnoid surface

shortlist: Sjögren's Syndrome with Central Nervous System Involvement

shortlist.label: Multiple Sclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent episodes of neurological deficits with evidence of inflammation and white matter changes, high titer of cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody, and CSF analysis showing 4 oligoclonal bands

shortlist.label: Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent episodes of neurological deficits, presence of white matter changes, and inflammation in the central nervous system

shortlist.label: Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis
shortlist.why_kept: Extensive white matter changes with enhancement along the arachnoid surface, and history of recurrent neurological deficits

shortlist.label: Primary Central Nervous System Vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Inflammation and white matter changes, with negative results for systemic vasculitis and other autoimmune disorders

shortlist.label: Sjögren's Syndrome with Central Nervous System Involvement
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of lymphocytes and plasma cells in brain biopsy, and history of recurrent neurological deficits

shortlist.label: Susac's Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent episodes of neurological deficits, with evidence of inflammation and white matter changes in the central nervous system

shortlist.label: Balo's Concentric Sclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: Extensive white matter changes with enhancement along the arachnoid surface, and history of recurrent neurological deficits

shortlist.label: Tumefactive Demyelinating Lesions
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of extensive white matter changes, and history of recurrent neurological deficits with inflammation

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with recurrent neurological symptoms, such as mild aphasia, confusion, right leg weakness, and right facial droop, along with the presence of oligoclonal bands in the CSF and extensive white matter changes on MRI, are consistent with a diagnosis of Multiple Sclerosis. The high titer of cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody may also suggest an autoimmune component.

rejected.label: Primary Central Nervous System Vasculitis
rejected.why: No evidence of vasculitis on pathological tests and no vascular abnormality on MRA

rejected.label: Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder
rejected.why: Lack of optic neuritis and spinal cord involvement

rejected.label: Acute Disseminated Encephalomyelitis
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms were recurrent and not monophasic, and the MRI findings were not typical of ADEM

rejected.label: Sjögren's Syndrome with Central Nervous System Involvement
rejected.why: No mention of sicca symptoms or other systemic features of Sjögren's Syndrome

rejected.label: Susac's Syndrome
rejected.why: No evidence of branch retinal artery occlusions or other characteristic features of Susac's Syndrome

rejected.label: Balo's Concentric Sclerosis
rejected.why: The MRI findings did not show the characteristic concentric rings of demyelination

rejected.label: Tumefactive Demyelinating Lesions
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and MRI findings were not typical of a large, tumefactive demyelinating lesion
